purpose: a per-runtime qualification vector Q_r and one substantive eligibility predicate, so a partial result can never be diluted by siblings that passed (external review point 8); the corrected EvE A0.1 label PARTIAL -- 5/14 measured, never PASS (point 2); and the redefinition D2 asks for: T_A1 (harness-attested A0.1, A0.2 mechanism + bridge, closure, frozen MRC) with the old lenient vector renamed T_exploratory and scoped to integration/pilot/debug only

review_basis.point_2: A0.1 for EvE must read `PARTIAL -- 5/14 measured`, never `PASS`
review_basis.point_8: a single global A0 PASS is the wrong output; Q_r and Eligible(r) = f(Q_r)
review_basis.D1: an interpreter mismatch is its own verdict (EXECUTION_ENV_DRIFT), never 'the evaluator behaviour disagrees' -- landed
review_basis.D2: the strict/literal threshold pair is replaced by T_A1; the lenient vector is renamed T_exploratory and scoped to integration/pilot/debug
review_basis.D3: identity is a harness measurement with fail-closed omission -- landed; this predicate reads its output (`measurement-attestation`) and fails closed

two_axes.what: since D3 the conformance runner keeps two axes apart, and Q_r must not merge them: the MEASUREMENT axis (`a0_1_measured` + `a0_1_adapted`) is whether the runtime's own evaluator interface produced a fresh verdict the runner compared against E*; the ACCEPTANCE axis (`a0_1_attested`) is whether the row echoes the harness measurement token and attests the bytes it executed.
two_axes.why_it_matters: KAPSO, EvE and Loreley agree with E* on the measurement surface (14/14, 14/14 and 5/14 measured) and are nonetheless non-accepting: 14 x MISSING_ATTESTATION. Folding that into the measurement component would report 'this runtime's measurement is wrong' when the truth is 'this runtime's evidence is missing'. A measurement error and a missing token are different findings with different remedies.
two_axes.runner_vocabulary: the runner states the same separation: a0_1.basis ('the attestation verdict is a separate axis: it decides whether the row is acceptable evidence, never whether the runtime measured it'), and the E-r-equals-E-star check's `measurement_agreeing` / `measurement_disagreeing_candidates` fields.
two_axes.in_q_r: `a0_1_measured.state` is derived from `rows[].verdict_before_attestation` and is the measurement state; the runner's folded state/label (which since D3 includes the acceptance axis) is carried as `runner_acceptance_state` on the same component. `a0_1_attested` carries the acceptance verdict.

provenance_classes.read_from_source: the value is read out of a stored artifact produced by another workstream
provenance_classes.inferred: derived by rule from other components, not directly observed

component_domains.a0_1_measured: `<measured>/<total>`; `state` in PASS | PARTIAL | FAIL | PENDING | BLOCKED. `state` is the MEASUREMENT axis; `runner_acceptance_state` carries the runner's folded state, which since D3 also folds in the acceptance axis

attested_a0_1.owner: a0/qualification/** is the CONSUMER of these records. The producer is the D3 workstream (a0/envelope/** + a0/conformance/**); this file declares the interface so the consumer can be checked before the producer exists.
attested_a0_1.why: Decision D3: behavioural agreement over C* cannot establish implementation identity. The mutant fixture in a0/fixtures/observational-equivalence/ reproduces an E' that agrees with E* bit-for-bit on all 14 candidates and is accepted by the behavioural checker, including when it omits the identity fields entirely. Identity must therefore become a HARNESS measurement: the harness owns the reference value and issues an OID measurement token (a0/envelope/envelope.py), the runtime still evaluates through its own evaluator path, it must submit an attestation of the bytes it executed, and the A0.1 row is accepted only when the harness compares its reference against the runtime-attested outcome AND the attestation's identity fields are present AND the identity check passes. Omission must fail.
attested_a0_1.in_one_line: absent record, or a record that omits the executed-bytes identity or the identity verdict, is UNPROVEN -- never PASS, never inferred from behaviour

domain_rule.PASS: a source decided, every declared field is present and non-empty, and the verdict is positive
domain_rule.FAIL: a source decided and the verdict is negative. NOT_SUBMITTED / MISSING_ATTESTATION / MISSING_IDENTITY / MISMATCH_ATTESTATION are all FAIL: the runtime was asked and did not answer with a usable identity. FAIL is never a soft pass either
domain_rule.UNPROVEN: no source decided for this runtime, or a source was present but did not establish anything (e.g. the run was made with the token requirement off). UNPROVEN fails T_A1

record_sources.why: PREFERRED, and the form the D3 runner actually produces (a0/conformance/conformance.py, check_id `measurement-attestation`, emitted by evaluate_runtime). `required` says whether the token requirement was ON for the run; `ok` is the runner's own per-runtime verdict; `envelope` names the harness run and nonce; the candidate lists name exactly which rows failed closed. A record carried by the run that produced the A0.1 report needs no separate report pin.
a per-runtime attestation block, if the runner is wired to carry one there instead of as a check
a standalone per-runtime record next to the runner, for a harness that cannot write inside report.json
the D3 envelope workstream's own output directory
the consumer's own drop box, so a wiring record can be placed by hand if the producer writes somewhere else

attested_a0_1.selection_rule: sources are tried in the order listed and the first one that DECIDES wins. A source may only decide with a positive or negative verdict and all the identity material present; a source that is present but inconclusive (token requirement off, missing metadata, verdict outside the declared domain) is recorded as rejected and the next source is tried. A standalone file record must additionally pin the current a0/conformance/report.json sha256, so the A0.1 re-run invalidates stale attestations instead of letting them outlive the run they describe.
forbidden_shortcuts: inferring identity from behavioural agreement on C* (this is the mutant fixture's whole point)
an adapter self-report with no harness-owned reference or OID token
treating a missing attestation as 'the runtime is fine'
treating a run made with the token requirement OFF as attested: `required=false` is UNPROVEN
replacing the runtime's own evaluation path with a harness subprocess: the runtime must still evaluate, the harness supplies the reference and the token (see a0/envelope/README.md)
attested_a0_1.status_now: LANDED AND DECIDED. The D3 harness issues the tokens (a0/envelope/**) and the conformance runner emits the per-runtime `measurement-attestation` check; the A0.1 report on record is that re-run with the envelope REQUIRED. The resolution now decides for all four runtimes, and the predicted source path (`runtimes.<r>.checks[check_id=measurement-attestation]`) matched the real output with no change to this contract: SimpleLoop = PASS (14/14 rows echo the token and attest the bytes they executed), KAPSO/EvE/Loreley = FAIL (MISSING_ATTESTATION on 14/14 rows, because the requirement was ON and their lanes did not answer). The measurement axis is unaffected -- the numbers agree -- so R_A1^main = ['simpleloop'] and the three others are out on R3_a0_1_attested, not on a measurement rule. Whether they are wired or explicitly excluded is open decision G6 in a0/qualification/freeze.py.
attested_a0_1.consumer_check: python3 a0/qualification/build_qualification.py --check ; python3 a0/qualification/eligibility.py --main-arm ; python3 a0/qualification/freeze.py gates

c_measure_vs_c_adapt.C_adapt: can the ADAPTER supply the semantics that interface cannot represent?
c_measure_vs_c_adapt.not_about_adapters_in_the_loop: this distinction is about a semantic gap in the runtime's interface -- all four runtimes run through an adapter, so 'the adapter is in the loop' is not the point. An adapted row is evidence for C_adapt and never for C_measure
c_measure_vs_c_adapt.a1_consequence: EvE's native numbers must not be used in any statistic that has to distinguish `invalid`/`error` from a genuine zero: on those rows EvE's interface returns a synthetic 0.0 and only the adapter's side-channel reading restores the verdict

predicate.name: Eligible
predicate.signature: Eligible(r; T) : Q_r x thresholds -> {eligible, not_eligible}

rules.expr: a0_1_measured.total > 0 and a0_1_measured.measured + a0_1_adapted.adapted == a0_1_measured.total and a0_1_measured.state in {'PASS','PARTIAL'}
rules.what: every row of C* is accounted for, nothing failed, and the split is not empty
rules.fail_closed: a missing row, a zero total, a FAIL state or an absent component is not eligible

rules.what: enough rows were measured by the RUNTIME'S OWN evaluator interface (C_measure), not merely supplied by the adapter (C_adapt). `T_A1` requires all of them; an adapted row is evidence for C_adapt and never for C_measure
rules.fail_closed: an absent measured/total counts as 0 and fails

rules.what: no row was accepted on an undeclared non-fresh number
rules.fail_closed: an absent adapted count reads as 0 only when the component itself is present

rules.what: the harness that owns the reference value also holds a submitted attestation of the bytes the runtime executed, and the identity check on those bytes passed. This is the clause D3 adds: behaviour alone cannot establish implementation identity, so identity must be a harness measurement and its omission must fail
rules.fail_closed: no record, or a record that omits the executed-bytes identity or the identity verdict, reads as UNPROVEN and fails every vector except one that explicitly allows UNPROVEN

rules.what: the runtime consumes scores per its claimed selection semantics (mechanism level)
rules.fail_closed: UNPROVEN -- and an absent component -- fails

rules.what: the same score->selection path was exercised inside the runtime's OWN real campaign (not only in a seam scenario): the frozen evaluator's score reached the runtime's selection state and moved the search
rules.fail_closed: an attempted-but-uncompleted round is ATTEMPTED, never PASS

rules.what: no autonomous external acquisition in the posture the runtime would run under
rules.fail_closed: an unreconciled closure record is CONDITIONAL at best and OPEN if no mechanism was probed

rules.what: the model route (MRC*) is frozen: the covering declaration validates against the external route registry, so two A1 arms can be asserted to be on the same declared route
rules.fail_closed: an unvalidated or absent declaration is ABSENT/PRESENT_UNFROZEN and fails T_A1

T_A1.scope: the vector that `Eligible(r)` means. `eligible=true` here is the licence to put this runtime's numbers into an A1 statistic.
T_A1.rationale: every clause names evidence this study is able to produce, and each was chosen because D2 asks for it: the runtime's OWN evaluator interface must have measured every row of C* (fraction 1.0, so an adapted row is not a measurement); the A0.1 row must carry a HARNESS attestation of the bytes the runtime executed (behaviour alone cannot establish implementation identity -- see the observational-equivalence mutant); A0.2 must be proven at mechanism level AND exercised in the runtime's own real campaign (the bridge); closure must be probe-proven, not reachable-by-a-posture; and the model route must be frozen.

T_exploratory.scope: integration / pilot / debug ONLY. This is the renamed former `T_literal` and it keeps that vector's leniency on purpose: it exists so a half-instrumented runtime can be driven while its evidence is still being produced. It is NOT a weaker main arm.
must_not_be_used_for: any statistic whose delta is reported as a study result
T_exploratory.fail_is_never_softened: UNPROVEN is tolerated here (the evidence has not been produced yet); FAIL is not. An axis that was decided AGAINST the runtime -- a contradicting attestation, an open closure, an unproven mechanism -- stays decided under every vector. Leniency is about missing evidence, never about rejected evidence.
T_exploratory.rationale: any native measurement counts (>= 1 row), the A0.2 mechanism check is still required because a pilot on an unproven selection mechanism measures nothing, an ATTEMPTED round is enough to exercise the plumbing, a closure that is reachable by a named posture is enough to run a pilot in, and the route may still be in flux.

predicate.exclusion_is_not_permanent: r not-in R_A1^main while any component is unmet. It is not a judgement on the runtime: it names missing evidence, and the runtime re-enters the moment the evidence exists
predicate.screen_is_a_different_object: `|R_1| >= 1` (plan:490) is a CANDIDATE SCREEN over runtimes: it answers 'may the study continue at all?'. Eligible(r) answers 'may THIS runtime's numbers be used in an A1 statistic?'. They are not the same object, and `|R_1| >= 1` does not imply that any runtime is in R_A1^main

screen.what: the candidate screen, not the eligibility predicate
screen.screen_source: a0/conformance/report.json#verdicts (the runner owns the A0.1 half)
screen.screen_uses: the runner's ACCEPTANCE state (PASS), so a runtime that measured every row but did not attest it is not in r_1_a0_1_only
screen.r_1_derived_note: DERIVED here from `a0_1_measured.state in {PASS, PARTIAL} and a0_2_mechanism == PASS`, i.e. from the MEASUREMENT axis, which is deliberately not the screen's axis; the authoritative A0.2 judgement is owned by the A0.2 workstream (a0/acceptance), so treat this as an upper bound on R_1
screen.screen_rule: |R_1| >= 1 suffices to continue (plan:490); a0_1_only is not R_1, which also needs A0.2
screen.not_the_same_as_eligibility: a runtime can be in the screen set and still not in R_A1^main. In the other direction the axes must not be mixed: a runtime whose MEASUREMENT is complete but whose ACCEPTANCE failed (KAPSO, Eve, Loreley: 14 x MISSING_ATTESTATION) is out of both, and the reason it is out is R3_a0_1_attested, never a measurement rule
